extracted.intended_audience: defense managers, military health services analysts, graduate students and researchers studying DoD productivity and contracting (OMB A-76) issues
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and measurement of productivity and efficiency in Department of Defense military health care delivery (analysis of Composite Work Unit, proposed Health Care Unit, Uniform Chart of Accounts, and application of OMB Circular A-76 and Efficiency Review policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of current performance against pre-established mission objectives (goals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by DoD guidance as one of the four important types of measures to be used in measuring organizational performance; used to assess whether mission objectives are being met rather than resource consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of current performance against either a pre-established standard or actual performance of a prior period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine how efficiently resources are being used; distinguished from effectiveness (which measures attainment of objectives) and labor productivity (which compares performance across periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor Productivity Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of performance during two periods of time (usually current period and a previous base period); compares actual manpower expended and resulting products produced or services rendered to disclose labor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A labor-produced index is the type of productivity index most frequently developed in DOD because labor is universally required; used for trend and period-to-period comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to Pre-established Standards (productivity vs. standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of labor performance against pre-established standards; compares actual manpower expenses on a job or task during a given period with the standard established for the job or task for that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a fourth class of productivity measure in DoD guidance; applicable where objective standards can be defined for tasks or jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Defense Productivity Program Policy Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Program will direct management attention on achieving maximum Defense outputs within available resource levels; productivity measurement, enhancement and evaluation will be an integral element of resource management; benefits of productivity enhancement should be reutilized at the lowest level practical to provide an incentive for management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policy statements (from DOD Directive 5010.31) set long-range objectives for integrating productivity measurement into resource management and incentivizing local managers to pursue labor-cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD Instruction 5010.34 operational requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish requirement for productivity goals at all levels; requirements for productivity measurement reporting and evaluation; guidance on work methods, workload measurement, and productivity-enhancing capital investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction provides operational direction for implementing the DOD Productivity Program, including using productivity indicators, accumulating productivity data, using productivity data in manpower development, and implementing measurement and evaluation systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested indicators for medical function (Enclosure guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested indicators for hospitals and clinics are the 'Health Care Composite Unit' and the 'Adjusted Admission Equivalent (USAF)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD enclosure on productivity measurement explicitly recommends these composite workload/output indicators as the suggested metrics for medical/hospital and clinic functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses of the Composite Work Unit (CWU)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CWU is used as a productivity/output measure and resource allocator across military medical facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis documents historical uses of the CWU (budgeting, reporting, trend analysis, resource allocation) and provides examples (Composite Work Unit tables for services and comparisons across years) showing how CWU has been applied inside DoD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticisms of the Composite Work Unit (CWU)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CWU has notable criticisms concerning reliability and representativeness as a productivity measure for military health care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis includes discussion and critique sections listing problems with CWU (biases, failure to capture case-mix and workload differences, sensitivity issues) and references critical analyses (e.g., 'The Composite Work Unit as a Resource Allocator: A Critical Analysis').

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Care Unit (HCU) design goals and formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a Health Care Unit as a proposed alternative to the CWU with a formulation approach, weighting schemes, and refinement to improve representativeness and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HCU section covers approach and formulation, approaches to weights, designer's final recommendation, initial refinement, and present HCU; includes proposed performance indicator(s) and recommended weights for outpatient and inpatient performance factors (appendices give factor weights and refined HCU weights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approaches to weighting performance factors (HCU & indices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit selection and calibration of outpatient and inpatient performance factor weights (e.g., outpatient performance factor weights, inpatient performance factor weights, refined HCU weights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thesis provides appendices and tables (Outpatient Performance Factor Weights, Inpatient Performance Factor Weights, Refined HCU Weights) and discusses methods (cost/disp vs length-of-stay relationships) to determine factor weights and index ranges for facility categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Chart of Accounts (UCA) objectives/features
rubrics_metrics.description: The UCA enhances cost awareness; provides more accurate and complete expense information; assigns expense responsibility to appropriate work centers; provides for categorization of management cost effectiveness; facilitates interpretation of cost consideration in the decision making process; provides for a more meaningful work count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UCA is presented as a complementary reporting/accounting framework (not a full cost-accounting system); it collects and reports expenses, maps expenses to work centers/programs, and is designed to improve expense transparency and decision support even though many UCA accounts do not correspond to specific organizational units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of the Uniform Chart of Accounts (UCA)
rubrics_metrics.description: UCA is not an expense and workload collection system, many UCA accounts do not correspond to specific organizational units, and cost objectives are not designed to support activity management needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis warns users that while UCA enhances cost awareness it lacks many characteristics of a full cost accounting system and may not directly support granular activity management or control over ancillary service costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-76 policy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for acquiring commercial or industrial products and services needed by the Government (A-76) require competition/cost-comparison for commercial activities and prescribe use of performance work statements and efficiency reviews for contracting-out decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis references OMB Circular A-76 (1976, revised 1979) as the primary federal policy for contracting out commercial activities and ties it to DOD Commercial Activities Program and Efficiency Review processes; it cites OMB A-76's role in determining when to buy vs. buy-in-house through cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency Review (ER) Program criteria and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of efficiency reviews and performance work statements to determine potential commercial contracting of activities and to identify operational improvements and resource determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis examines the ER Program, related memoranda (e.g., 'Use of Performance Work Statements and Efficiency Reviews, 27 November 1981'), draft instructions (DOD 5010.xxxx), and implementation guidance (e.g., Chief of Naval Operations letter), and summarizes practical implementation concerns and potential savings findings from GAO and other studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and reporting obligations for productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to develop and use productivity indicators, accumulate productivity data, utilize productivity and performance data in manpower requirements development, and implement productivity measurement and evaluation reporting to Federal systems (e.g., BLS and annual Federal Productivity Report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD instructions require ongoing data collection, reporting, and integration of productivity metrics into planning/programming/budgeting processes; enclosure guidance names the outputs expected and the channels for reporting (federal productivity reporting system).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicator/index design (input-output relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity measure should be a productivity index: the relationship between the volume of goods produced or services rendered and the quantity of resources consumed, permitting period-to-period comparison of the input-output relationship of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD guidance emphasizes labor-producer indices and major function indices to determine productivity coverage; indices should support comparisons across activities, facilities, and time periods and feed into resource allocation and budgeting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted Admission Equivalent (AAE) and other workload measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Adjusted Admission Equivalent (USAF) and other adjusted workload counts as alternative/comparative workload-output measures to CWU for hospitals and inpatient services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis includes exhibits and appendices comparing AAE, CWU, Comparative Services Indexes and other workload measures and discusses where AAE may be more representative or comparable for certain facility types or analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of indices and index ranges by facility category
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and interpret ranges of indices for facility categories (e.g., ranges of indices for Category I facilities) to help classify performance and identify outliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thesis appendices provide example ranges and recommend interpreting index values relative to defined category ranges to assess facility performance and to refine targets and weights in HCU/CWU construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design trade-offs and limitations when creating productivity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize trade-offs such as simplicity vs. representativeness, data availability vs. desired granularity, accounting limitations, and incentives created by chosen measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the thesis the authors emphasize that any composite metric (CWU, HCU) will have limitations and potential distortions; design should account for data quality, accounting boundaries, wartime/peacetime differences, and unintended managerial incentives.
